metadata.name: IMPROV PERCS 072 1 BAR 130 BPM.wav
metadata.description: This 48KHz/24bit stereo sample pack contains 70 loops (68Mb) of improvised percussion instruments at 130BPM. Sources were placed on the studio floor and played with two regular drumsticks. A central AKG C414 in omni config through NPNG preamp was the closest mic. Two Josephson C617s through Millennia Media preamps captured the room ambience. Sources included water bottles, large vacuum cleaner pipes, wood offcuts, food containers and various other objects which were never meant to be used like this. All sources were recorded into Pro Tools through Frontier Design Group converters and large amounts of Beat Detective were employed to make something decent out of our terrible playing. Final processing was carried out in Cool Edit Pro. Recorded by Brady Leduc and myself at Pulsworks Audio Arts.

Four layers of the sample were used in an NN-XT Sampler (Reason), each layer with different loop start & end points (generally 0.4% apart). Layers use the same keyspan, the sampler is set to alternate between layers.

metadata.name: Arp.wav
metadata.description: This is a synth sound I programmed using Reason's Thor polyphonic synthesizer to use on a Freesound "Dare" colaboration project. I used two oscs with phase modulation to produce this sound. I then used the matrix pattern sequencer to programme an arp. This file is a four bar loop in D-minor at 90bpm.

metadata.name: Arp & Co.wav
metadata.description: This is two synth sounds to use on a Freesound "Dare" colaboration project. I programmed the first using Reason's Thor polyphonic synthesizer. I used two oscs with phase modulation to produce one sound. I then used the matrix pattern sequencer to programme an arp. The other sound uses Rob Papens Predator synth. I used the self oscilation feature. By turning off the oscs and turning up the resonance in the filter you can make it self oscilate producing some interesting and unusual sounds! I also used the sequencer in Predator. This file is a four bar loop in D-minor at 90bpm.

metadata.name: 160bpm groove -4.wav
metadata.description: a selection of drum and bass loops that I made myself with 'ableton live sequencing software'. - using the impulse drum machine, reverb, filter delay, compressor 2, resonators, gate, saturator, EQ and ping pong. I drew the drum pattern out in matrix editor and changed the cutoff and frequency, transparency, drive, stretch, delay, volume, and transpose of drum sounds from my own copyright free sound library, and then ran each sound through various effects and processors mentioned above randomly, had fun, messed around, mixed up, deleted and added then settled on something that i liked the sound of and then rendered into a wav file and uploaded here to share! :)

metadata.name: Matt's House Kick Drum 120 BPM
metadata.description: This is just a simple four to the floor kick drum pattern at 120 bpm. I created the kick itself by layering various synth timbres in Rob Papen's Albino plugin. Processing was also applied such as compression, EQ and using subtle distortion in specific frequency areas to get it sounding like this. For anyone that would like to hear my music: https://soundcloud.com/mattcmusic

metadata.name: 20140306_attackloop_120BPM_4_4_23rd_century_loop1b.flac
metadata.description: This is a loop created with the Waldorf Attack VST Drum Synth. The kit used was 23rd century Kit and the loop was created using Cubase 7.5. The following plugins were used to process the signal: AnarchRhythms, StepFilter, Guitar Rig 5 and iZotome Ozone 5. The different variants gradually change to more an more deep frequencies. 8 variations are labelled form a till h. Everything is at 120 bpm and measure 4/4. Enjoy!

metadata.name: Audacity_Loop_120bpm.wav
metadata.description: This is a loop created using Audacity for dare-29. http://www.freesound.org/forum/dare-the-community/35414/ First I created a click track in Audacity, at 120 BPM 4/4. The I loaded the bassdrum. I added another sound to the bassdrum to create variation in the bar and 1/2 bar hits. Followed by the hihats. - I used a pre-made hihat pattern, but I cut it up and reassembled parts of it to create my own pattern (including a reversed hit and one I stretched in Audacity using the build in Paulstrewtch). Then I loaded a clap and the snare and placed these sounds to create a pattern. I also used Audacity volume envelopt to shorten one of the snare hits to fit the mix better. I finished off by placing the cymbal and the metal rattle to add interest to the loop. No other effects were used (besides Paulstretch mentioned above) and reversing and volume envelope (if you actually consider those as envelopes). Everything was done in Audacity and the mixing was achieved simply by adjusting the volume of some of the samples, as needed. Sounds used: http://www.freesound.org/people/mishicu/sounds/195747/ http://www.freesound.org/people/OwlStorm/sounds/209015/ http://www.freesound.org/people/Sound1A/sounds/146351/ http://www.freesound.org/people/young_daddy/sounds/24787/ http://www.freesound.org/people/it_was_the_sun/sounds/209513/ http://www.freesound.org/people/Alteration/sounds/191490/ http://www.freesound.org/people/jorickhoofd/sounds/160047/

metadata.name: convoluted back to back loop 60 bpm 1a.wav
metadata.description: This is loop 1 in a series of 40 loops that belong together. They all have a deep dubspace feel at 60 bpm and belong to the "Convoloops pack 01 - back to back dubspace 60 bpm" sample pack. They all have the same name: "convoluted back to back loop 60 bpm" with a number and letter suffix (1a till 5h). Each group with the same number but with different letters are based on the same sounds and feel. The most rhythmic ones are these with suffix a till d and these with e till h are more effects. They were created using the microtonik VSTi. I took the back to back preset and convoluted it with some variations of itself. After this process I added some more convolution with another SIR, a resonator effect from MHC, and some more character with (you never guess it) the excellent Character plugin from my TC powercore firewire. All this was done within Cubase SX. After that I mastered these loops within Wavelab using several plugins: fades, equalising, multiband compressing, limiting & dither.

They all have the same name: "convoluted back to back loop 60 bpm" with a number and letter suffix (1a till 5h). metadata.name: convoluted bare bone loop 60 bpm 011.wav
metadata.description: This is loop 1 in a series of 135 loops that belong together. They all have a deep dubspace feel in 1 bar 4/4 at 60 bpm and belong to the "Convoloops pack 02 - bare bone dubspace 60 bpm" sample pack. They all have the same name: "convoluted bare bone loop 60 bpm" with three numbers as suffix. The first of the three numbers indicates a group of samples with a similar sound and feel. The most rhythmic ones are these with 1 till 4 as last number in the suffix and these with 5 till 8 are more effects. Finally number 9 as the last number in the suffix is the start of the delay and/or reverb tail of the previous loop. The second number separates variations in pitch of the initial loop before any processing is applied. Of these variations number 5 is more granular & experimental. All loops were created using the microtonik VSTi. I took the bare bones preset and convoluted it with some variations of itself. After this process I added some more convolution with another SIR, some diffusion, delay & chorus with the Fusion Reflector ensemble from Native Instruments Reaktor, and some more character with (you never guess it) the excellent Character plugin from my TC powercore firewire. All this was done within Cubase SX. After that I mastered these loops within Wavelab using several plugins: fades, equalising, multiband compressing, limiting & dither.

They all have the same name: "convoluted bare bone loop 60 bpm" with three numbers as suffix. The first of the three numbers indicates a group of samples with a similar sound and feel. The most rhythmic ones are these with 1 till 4 as last number in the suffix and these with 5 till 8 are more effects. Finally number 9 as the last number in the suffix is the start of the delay and/or reverb tail of the previous loop. The second number separates variations in pitch of the initial loop before any processing is applied. Of these variations number 5 is more granular & experimental. All loops were created using the microtonik VSTi. I took the bare bones preset and convoluted it with some variations of itself. After this process I added some more convolution with another SIR, some diffusion, delay & chorus with the Fusion Reflector ensemble from Native Instruments Reaktor, and some more character with (you never guess it) the excellent Character plugin from my TC powercore firewire. All this was done within Cubase SX. After that I mastered these loops within Wavelab using several plugins: fades, equalising, multiband compressing, limiting & dither.

metadata.name: ocea130_08_remix oo1.mp3
metadata.description: This is a remix of oceas 8th loop at 130bpm, the samples in this pack were made mostly by running the original loop through a custom plugin i made with synthedit. The general idea of the plugin is to seperate the incoming audio into 8 seperate channels using high-resonance bandpass filters, then run each of the 8 channels through its own special effect including reverb, delay, harmonic generation, ring modulation, modulation of the original signal by the harmonic generation signal out, and another reverb.

metadata.name: China Dream Convoloop a-00.wav
metadata.description: This rhythmic drone loop is one of the " Convoloops pack 03 - China Dream dronescapes 120 bpm" samplepack. These loops all belong together and are variations and alterations of each other. They all are 1 bar 4/4 long and have 120 bpm as tempo. They can be used as background loops for ambient music. Each loop has the same name with a letter an a number in the end. I took the microtonik VSTi within Cubase SX and exported the China Dream loop, which is four bars long, as 24 bit wav file. This file was then imported as impulse file within the freeware SIR convolution reverb and applied it to the original loop, all wet. So I convoluted a drumloop with itself! After that, two more reverb units were applied: another SIR (this time with an impulse file from one of the fabulous Spirit Canyon Audio CD's) and the excellent Classic Reverb from my TC Powercore Firewire (preset: Deep Space). Each of these reverbs was set all wet. When I did that, I got an 8 bar loop. This loop was then sliced up into 8 peaces of each 1 bar. So I got 8 short one bar loops: I numbered them with numbers 00 till 07. I repeated the whole process for several impulse files for the second SIR: the results are the variation a till r. There are two exceptions on the all wet rule: the two last loop sets, q and r, have their reverbs not set all wet, so these are the most rhythmic ones, since there is some of the original drumloop left. All the others are rhythmic but very vague. The most busy ones are each time numbers 03 and 04. 01 can be used as an intro and 07 is kind of the tail. All loops are normalised and mastered within Wavelab using several high quality plugins (EQ, multiband finaliser, limiter). Enjoy!

Each loop has the same name with a letter an a number in the end. I took the microtonik VSTi within Cubase SX and exported the China Dream loop, which is four bars long, as 24 bit wav file. This file was then imported as impulse file within the freeware SIR convolution reverb and applied it to the original loop, all wet. So I convoluted a drumloop with itself! After that, two more reverb units were applied: another SIR (this time with an impulse file from one of the fabulous Spirit Canyon Audio CD's) and the excellent Classic Reverb from my TC Powercore Firewire (preset: Deep Space). Each of these reverbs was set all wet. When I did that, I got an 8 bar loop. This loop was then sliced up into 8 peaces of each 1 bar. So I got 8 short one bar loops: I numbered them with numbers 00 till 07. I repeated the whole process for several impulse files for the second SIR: the results are the variation a till r. There are two exceptions on the all wet rule: the two last loop sets, q and r, have their reverbs not set all wet, so these are the most rhythmic ones, since there is some of the original drumloop left. All the others are rhythmic but very vague. The most busy ones are each time numbers 03 and 04. 01 can be used as an intro and 07 is kind of the tail. All loops are normalised and mastered within Wavelab using several high quality plugins (EQ, multiband finaliser, limiter). Enjoy!

Each loop has the same name with a letter an a number in the end. I took the microtonik VSTi within Cubase SX and exported the China Dream loop, which is four bars long, as 24 bit wav file. This file was then imported as impulse file within the freeware SIR convolution reverb and applied it to the original loop, all wet. So I convoluted a drumloop with itself! After that, two more reverb units were applied: another SIR (this time with an impulse file from one of the fabulous Spirit Canyon Audio CD's) and the excellent Classic Reverb from my TC Powercore Firewire (preset: Deep Space). Each of these reverbs was set all wet. When I did that, I got an 8 bar loop. This loop was then sliced up into 8 peaces of each 1 bar. So I got 8 short one bar loops: I numbered them with numbers 00 till 07. I repeated the whole process for several impulse files for the second SIR: the results are the variation a till r. There are two exceptions on the all wet rule: the two last loop sets, q and r, have their reverbs not set all wet, so these are the most rhythmic ones, since there is some of the original drumloop left. All the others are rhythmic but very vague. The most busy ones are each time numbers 03 and 04. 01 can be used as an intro and 07 is kind of the tail. All loops are normalised and mastered within Wavelab using several high quality plugins (EQ, multiband finaliser, limiter). Enjoy!

Each loop has the same name with a letter an a number in the end. I took the microtonik VSTi within Cubase SX and exported the China Dream loop, which is four bars long, as 24 bit wav file. This file was then imported as impulse file within the freeware SIR convolution reverb and applied it to the original loop, all wet. So I convoluted a drumloop with itself! After that, two more reverb units were applied: another SIR (this time with an impulse file from one of the fabulous Spirit Canyon Audio CD's) and the excellent Classic Reverb from my TC Powercore Firewire (preset: Deep Space). Each of these reverbs was set all wet. When I did that, I got an 8 bar loop. This loop was then sliced up into 8 peaces of each 1 bar. So I got 8 short one bar loops: I numbered them with numbers 00 till 07. I repeated the whole process for several impulse files for the second SIR: the results are the variation a till r. There are two exceptions on the all wet rule: the two last loop sets, q and r, have their reverbs not set all wet, so these are the most rhythmic ones, since there is some of the original drumloop left. All the others are rhythmic but very vague. The most busy ones are each time numbers 03 and 04. 01 can be used as an intro and 07 is kind of the tail. All loops are normalised and mastered within Wavelab using several high quality plugins (EQ, multiband finaliser, limiter). Enjoy!
